title: vendored_scan's grep follows the reader's locale: under a UTF-8 locale BSD grep drops a matching line holding an invalid byte, so neutral.bats can pass one
body:
Found by dc on 2026-10-23 while building 0203, from critic-shell's warning on its new documentation.bats arm, and confirmed by vc the same day.

`vendored_scan` (tests/lib/vendored_set.bash:35 and :37) runs `grep -a` under whatever locale its caller has. Nothing in the harness pins one: tests/lib/ sets `LC_ALL=C` only on single sorts, and `lib/cmd/test` sets none. vc measured it on rhadamanth with BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD (`/usr/bin/grep`). The input was a two-line file whose second line holds the pattern and a 0xFF byte:

- `LC_ALL=C grep -a -n -E client`: rc 0, and the line is printed.
- `LC_ALL=en_GB.UTF-8 grep -a -n -E client`: rc 1, and nothing is printed.

**Why it matters.** neutral.bats scans the vendored set through `vendored_scan` for names, citations and decision language. Run under a UTF-8 locale on macOS, it passes a vendored line that matches but holds an invalid byte: a false green. The agent shell sets `LC_ALL=C`, so no agent's run sees it. hv's terminal is en_GB.UTF-8, and a cut's `test all` gate runs there. dc measured that CI's Ubuntu GNU grep prints the line. `vendored_shown`'s comment filter (:68, `grep -a -v`) reads under the same locale. The defect is latent: the vendored text is ASCII today, but nothing holds it to ASCII.

**Fix.** Put `LC_ALL=C` on each grep in tests/lib/vendored_set.bash, as 0203's new documentation.bats arm already does (`LC_ALL=C grep -a`). That arm then scans through `vendored_scan` instead of carrying its own copy of the rule, so the rule has one home. No new arm is added: the measurement above is the evidence, and a test of the scan helper would be a test of a test.

Done when: every grep in tests/lib/vendored_set.bash reads under `LC_ALL=C`; documentation.bats's Homebrew arm scans through `vendored_scan`; the six tree scans and help pass under BSD and GNU tools, run with `LC_ALL=en_GB.UTF-8` so the run has the locale the fix pins against; and the fix has landed in the 0.1.13 batch.

## Resolution

Fixed at cedb2455 in the 0.1.13 batch, on landing suite 20261023-2029 at 23f5f70e (2435 of 2435 ok, 5 skips, seal empty) (dc built it on 0203's tip, 85b2b029; vc landed it).

- Every grep in tests/lib/vendored_set.bash reads with -a under LC_ALL=C. vendored_drop, new, is the one filter over a scan's hits: vendored_shown's comment filter and both of installhints.bats's filters call it. neutral.bats's two awks over hits read under C too. documentation.bats's Homebrew arm (0203's) reads its docs, and its floor, through vendored_scan. So the rule has one home.
- vendored_scan, vendored_shown and vendored_drop answer 2, never a clean scan, when given no file or an output they cannot write. A failed redirection exits 1, grep's "no match", and main's vendored_scan returned 0 in each such case.
- Measured on rhadamanth:
  - BSD grep 2.6.0 under en_GB.UTF-8, with -a, drops a matching line holding a 0xFF byte when the byte comes before the match, or when the pattern must read past it.
  - BSD and GNU 3.12 alike miss one whose pattern must read the byte, under en_GB.UTF-8 and C.UTF-8.
  - macOS awk exits 2 on such a hit under en_GB.UTF-8.
  - Under C, every one of these reads the line.
- No new arm, as the issue said. The changed Homebrew arm is red on main (README.md:241) and green at the fix, under BSD and GNU tools, in C and in en_GB.UTF-8. The tree scans, help and installhints.bats pass under BSD and GNU with LC_ALL=en_GB.UTF-8.
